messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: rapid OOM spike + node flaps on prod-serving (us-west-2). oom_kill_count > 50 in 5m on pool=kv-paged. auto-fallback to smaller variants triggered.

maya: I'm oncall, looking. seeing repeated `OOMKilled` + `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` in the runtime sidecar logs.

maya: quick log snip:
```
2026-03-17T02:12:05Z runtime ERROR: allocation failed: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED: requested 1.2GB, available 512MB
pid=4231 container=serving-worker model=llama-13b-quantized
kernel: paged-kv-allocator: fragmented free space -> unable to satisfy contiguous block
```

sahil: likely slow fragmentation (kv pages) leading to eventual allocation failure — we've seen this pattern: slow creep of paged slabs then sudden OOM on larger sequence lengths.

sahil: mitigation plan (fast): 1) route traffic away from models that use large contiguous KV allocations, 2) enable aggressive KV eviction on affected nodes, 3) restart affected pods on a drained node.

jordan: customer-ops: seeing ~2.3% 5xx on generation endpoints for a subset of customers in the region. a couple of paid customers opened chats. link to incident page: https://redwood/incident/1749970000

maya: starting with routing change: bump routing rule for prod-serving to prefer variant=llama-13b-small for new requests for 10m. invoking rollout: `redwoodctl route set --service prod-serving --prefer variant=llama-13b-small --duration 600s`

ops-bot: Action queued: route change applied to 12/14 nodes.

sahil: while traffic shifts, run targeted drain + restart on the two worst nodes: node-prod-3 and node-prod-7. commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon node-prod-3 && kubectl drain node-prod-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data && kubectl delete pod -l pool=kv-paged --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-prod-3 -n serving
```

maya: starting drains now. also toggling `kv_paged.evict_aggressiveness=high` via runtime flag on the affected nodes to force prefix/KV eviction earlier. will patch back after stabilization.

ops-bot: node-prod-3 drained, 9 pods rescheduled to node-prod-10 and node-prod-11. restart of serving-worker pods succeeded (restarts: 1).

jordan: customer-ops: customers on the affected shard updated: two customers reported degraded responses at ~02:13-02:20. CS is sending an ETA update and offering compensatory credits.

maya: after restart, CUDA allocation errors drop, OOM rate down to baseline (~0.04% in last 5m). metrics: memory fragmentation index (pager) dropped from 0.78 -> 0.41 on node-prod-3 post-restart.

sahil: temporary fixes applied: routing fallback, aggressive eviction, node drains. follow-ups: 1) implement a background slab defrag compaction job for kv-paged (low-priority, non-blocking), 2) add alert for fragmentation index > 0.6 sustained for 10m, 3) build safe auto-drain runbook for node-level fragment events.

dave: taking handoff — thanks @maya. I'll keep monitoring for the next 2h. next steps I'll kick off: schedule a controlled drain of node-prod-7 (still showing elevated frag), add an A/B test to validate `kv_paged.compact_on_idle=true` on canary nodes.

customer-ops: CS updated customers at 02:35. no new escalations.

maya: leaving notes in the incident doc and will open follow-up ticket: INF-3121 (kv-paged compaction task + alerting + postmortem).

dave: acked. monitoring looks stable; re-routing reduced 5xx to ~0.1%. closing on-call chat here, will update once follow-ups are created. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. next update due in 2 hours or on regress.
